label: Empty world: a world at which no individual, concrete or abstract, exists
definition: EmptyWorld m holds when some world of the model has no existing individual at all: every individual of the carrier, concrete or abstract, is absent there. NoEmptyWorld m is its negation: every world has some existing individual. A world lacking only the concrete individuals is weaker and is not an empty world in this sense. Example: OriginDeletion.Control.withEmpty (its sixth world). Counterexample: OriginToleranceIdentity.Control.faithful, where every world contains a or b. Distinguished from a concrete-empty moment of a history (InertEmptiness.ConcreteEmptyAt), which concerns presence at a time within one world, and from the absence of every actual individual, which allows other individuals to exist.
note: Analyst framework definition, attribution deferred, for testing the origin-tolerance rival against Arrival A. Whether a world with nothing is metaphysically possible is OPEN; the encoded origin-tolerance commitments neither assert nor exclude it.
